subject: Pilot wrap playbook — acceptance signals & test harness
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Chris Taylor <chris@brightgate.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot wrap playbook — acceptance signals & test harness

Hi Chris,

Thanks again for the demo last week — great discussion. As promised, I put together a single-note playbook to make the pilot wrap and evaluation phase deterministic for both teams. The goal is to define success signals, concrete exit gates, and the acceptance test harness so we can converge to a production decision on the proposed timeline.

Attached: pilot-acceptance-checklist.xlsx (workbook with KPIs + evidence owners)

High level ask: can you validate the acceptance targets below and confirm internal owners on your side so we can lock dates?

Proposed success signals (short):
- Latency: 95th percentile inference < 300ms for 1k token prompts under peak (burst) workload
- Throughput: sustained 60 qps with <5% error rate for 10 minutes
- Quality: token-concordance / exact match on canonical prompt set >= 92% (see evidence matrix)
- Security: SSO + session audit logs verified; no PII exfiltration in 1M-sample test

Exit gates (must be met to proceed to commit):
1) All infra smoke tests green (latency/throughput)
2) Acceptance test suite run and >= 92% on quality metrics
3) SOC2 evidence package and SSO flows validated
4) Mutual action plan signed by procurement for initial capacity (monthly commit)

Acceptance tests we propose to run during evaluation (examples):
- Load profile replay (10-minute peak windows, 3 repeats)
- Prompt concordance set (100 canonical prompts, blinded)
- Fault-injection: network jitter and degraded GPU perf to verify graceful fallback
- Data retention and deletion trace on sample payloads

Timeline (draft):
- MAP finalization: 2027-04-19
- Test runs and evidence collection: 2027-04-20 — 2027-04-28
- Go/no-go meeting (decision): 2027-04-29

Next steps: please confirm the targets above, provide your security contact for the SOC2 artifacts, and let me know who on procurement we should loop in. If that looks OK I will send a short MAP doc (task owners + dates) for signature.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: pilot-acceptance-checklist.xlsx (Excel workbook)]
From: Chris Taylor <chris@brightgate.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, procurement@brightgate.com
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 14:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Pilot wrap playbook — acceptance signals & test harness

Monica — thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifying Qs before we lock the MAP: 

1) For latency, are we measuring cold-start or warm (KV-cache populated)? We will need both numbers; operations will be sensitive to warm 95th.
2) The throughput target (60 qps) — is that with batching enabled? We need specifics (batch sizes and expected payload sizes).
3) On quality: the 92% concordance — is that strict exact-match or fuzzy similarity? Our product team prefers a weighted F1 for entity preservation.

Security: procurement looped in as requested. Our security lead is laura.kim@brightgate.com — she will need the SOC2 artifact list and a sample retention policy.

We can run the test window you proposed but may need to move the decision meeting to 2027-04-30 if we run into scheduling conflicts on our side.

Happy to take the MAP draft and evidence matrix.

—Chris
Chris Taylor
VP Product
BrightGate
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Chris Taylor <chris@brightgate.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot wrap playbook — acceptance signals & test harness

Chris — great questions, answered inline and attached a short MAP draft + evidence matrix.

1) Latency measurement: we report both cold-start and warm; for exit gate we require warm 95th < 300ms. Cold-start will be documented per deployment (canary vs full).
2) Throughput: 60 qps assumes batching at target batch size of 8 for 256-token avg payloads. I included the batch profile in the evidence sheet. If your payloads skew larger we can re-run with adjusted batch targets.
3) Quality: concordance is a blended metric — exact-match on core fields (70% weight) + semantic similarity on free text (30% weight). The evidence-matrix.csv includes scoring code and expected pass thresholds.

Attachments included: MAP-draft-v1.pdf (mutual action list + owners), evidence-matrix.csv (scoring and raw-vectors).

MAP draft (summary):
- 2027-04-19: MAP sign-off (owners: Chris / Monica / Jordan)
- 2027-04-20 — 04-28: Test runs (owners: BrightGate ops / Redwood SRE)
   - Test #1: Load replay (owner: BrightGate Ops)
   - Test #2: Concordance (owner: BrightGate Product)
   - Test #3: Security & retention checks (owner: BrightGate Security)
- 2027-04-29: Contingency day for re-runs
- 2027-04-30: Decision meeting (final sign-off)

Procurement: looping in procurement@brightgate.com (thanks Chris). On our side Marissa will own the pricing appendix and will prepare the contract chunk for an initial 6-month commit (flexible capacity).

Failure modes / fallbacks (important):
- If throughput < target but quality OK, we recommend increasing batch sizes + short-term dedicated GPU burst for cutover to production.
- If quality fails, we provide a rollback to smaller model variant and a defect triage cadence (24-hour SLA for critical fixes).

Please review the attached MAP-draft-v1.pdf and evidence matrix and tell us if the decision meeting needs to move to 04-30. If you can confirm laura.kim as security lead and procurement contact, I will send the formal MAP for signature.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
